polities.name: Ukrainian People's Republic (Central Rada)
polities.note: Proclaimed by the Third Universal on 20 Nov 1917 (autonomous within Russia), independent from the Fourth Universal of 22 Jan 1918; Kyiv, then Zhytomyr and Korosten in Feb 1918; abolished by the coup of 29 Apr 1918. Claimed the nine south-western governorates of the Russian Empire; Crimea was left out of the claim.

maps.t: Category: Maps of the Ukrainian People's Republic

polities.name: Ukrainian State (Second Hetmanate)
polities.note: 29 Apr to 14 Dec 1918, under hetman Pavlo Skoropadsky. Nine governorates (Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kharkiv, Podillia, Poltava, Volhynia, Kholm, Katerynoslav, Kherson) and two districts (Polissia, Tavria). Crimea and the Kuban were part of the state (the Wikipedia map shades them as its territory), so Crimea is in the footprint and the Kuban is three extra points. Other parts outside modern Ukraine (Kholm region, Podlachia, Brest, Gomel, Starodub) are extra points too.

polities.name: Ukrainian People's Republic (Directorate)
polities.note: Restored on 14 Dec 1918; capitals Kyiv, then Vinnytsia, Zhmerynka, Proskuriv, Rivne, Kamianets-Podilskyi. Controlled only the north of the Right Bank at first and, after the Act of Union (22 Jan 1919), claimed the West Ukrainian People's Republic as well. Government in exile from 12 Nov 1920. Footprints are the area actually held, drawn roughly.

phases.label: Right Bank and Eastern Galicia (Act of Union)

maps.t: Category: Maps of the Ukrainian People's Republic

polities.name: West Ukrainian People's Republic
polities.note: Proclaimed 1 Nov 1918 in Lviv (capital moved to Ternopil, then Stanislaviv); Eastern Galicia, Lemkivshchyna, Northern Bukovina and Transcarpathia were claimed; united with the UNR on 22 Jan 1919; lost to Poland by July 1919.

maps.t: Category: Maps of the Western Ukrainian People's Republic

polities.name: Ukrainian SSR (Soviet Ukraine)
polities.note: Proclaimed Dec 1917 and again Jan 1919; a founder of the USSR in 1922; capital Kharkiv until 1934, then Kyiv. Territory by date: 1922-39 without Galicia, Volhynia (west), Bukovina, Transcarpathia and Crimea (Crimean ASSR in the RSFSR); Sept 1939 Western Ukraine; 1940 Northern Bukovina and Southern Bessarabia; 1945 Transcarpathia; 1954 Crimea. English-language texts that say 'the Ukraine' usually mean this state.

polities.name: Carpatho-Ukraine
polities.note: Autonomous region of Czechoslovakia from Oct 1938, declared independence 15 Mar 1939 and was occupied by Hungary.

maps.t: Map of the Republic of Carpatho-Ukraine 1939.png
Category: Maps of the Carpathian Ukraine (1938-1939)

polities.name: Reichskommissariat Ukraine
polities.note: German civil administration 1941-44, capital Rivne. Galicia was part of the General Government, Transnistria went to Romania, Crimea was kept apart.

polities.name: Ukraine (independent)
polities.note: Within the borders of 1991 (Crimea included de jure).

polities.name: Crimean Khanate
polities.note: 1441-1783 (Ottoman vassal from 1478, annexed by Russia on 19 Apr 1783). Per the article: Crimea, the steppes of the northern Black Sea coast between the Danube and the Don, and the northern Kuban; the Nogai hordes (Budjak, Yedisan, Perekop, Kuban) were its vassals. Footprint: Crimea and the steppe south of 47.5 N, plus the Kuban as outside points. Crimea is part of the country (modern Ukraine); before 1954 it was not part of any Ukrainian state, so the Ukrainian-state footprints leave it out and this one holds it.

phases.label: Crimea and the Black Sea steppe

maps.t: The Crimean Khanate at its maximum extent (1525).png

polities.name: Golden Horde (Ukrainian steppe)
polities.note: Rough rule, not yet checked against Wikipedia: the steppe and forest-steppe south and east of the Rus principalities, from the Mongol conquest (1240) to the Khanate of Crimea (1441).

polities.name: Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia
polities.note: Rough rule, not yet checked against Wikipedia: Galicia, Volhynia and Podillia in the west.

polities.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (Ukrainian lands)
polities.note: Boundaries by date from the treaties (my own knowledge, not re-read on Wikipedia); the footprints are boxes on the grid. Lithuanian lands in Ukraine: Volhynia and Chernihiv-Siversk from the 1340s-60s, Kyiv and Podillia after the Blue Waters (1362); Podillia west to Poland 1430-34; Chernihiv-Siversk to Muscovy in 1503 (treaty of Moscow); Lublin 1569 moved Volhynia, Bratslav, Kyiv and Podlachia to the Polish Crown. Cells 55 and 56 (Dniester-Boh steppe, 48.25N 28-29E) added to 1362-1430 from the Historical Atlas of Ukraine map "Ukrainian lands circa 1400" (Lithuanian acquisitions of 1392). Cells 55-56 kept Lithuanian in 1430-1503 as Bratslav Land (Eastern Podolia), on the author's suggestion (MAPA atlas: Eastern Podolia under Lithuania). Cells 37 and 57 (Dniester, 47.75-48.25N 29.6E) added 1430-1569, cell 56 added 1503-1569: rough fill of a gap.

polities.name: Ottoman Empire (Ukrainian lands)
polities.note: Boundaries by date from the treaties (my own knowledge, not re-read on Wikipedia); the footprints are boxes on the grid. Black Sea coast and Budjak from the 1470s-80s (Kaffa 1475, Akkerman 1484); Podillia with Kamianets 1672-99 (Buchach to Karlowitz); Küçük Kaynarca 1774 and the fall of Ochakiv/Jassy 1791-92 pushed the border back to the Dniester; Budjak lost in 1812.

polities.name: Kyivan Rus and Galicia-Volhynia
polities.note: Rough rule of the pile territory: north of 48 N and west of 36 E.

polities.name: Cossack Hetmanate and Zaporozhian Sich
polities.note: Rough rule of the pile territory: the Dnipro region and the east, from 46.5 N.

polities.name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (Ukrainian lands)
polities.note: Boundaries by date from the treaties (my own knowledge, not re-read on Wikipedia); the footprints are boxes on the grid. Lublin 1569 (Volhynia, Bratslav, Kyiv to the Crown); Chernihiv-Siversk regained 1618 (Deulino); Khmelnytsky 1648 and Zboriv 1649 cut off the Dnipro lands; Andrusovo 1667 and the Eternal Peace 1686 left the Right Bank; Galicia to Austria 1772; Right Bank to Russia 1793, western Volhynia 1795. Ottoman Podillia 1672-99 is left out. Gap 1672.7-1699.1 filled: the Crown kept Volhynia, Lublin and Galicia while the Ottomans held Podillia (Buchach 1672, Karlowitz 1699). North-western Crown and Lithuanian lands (Volhynia, Lublin area, Polesia, cells north of 50.45N west of 28.9E and north of 51.5N west of 32E) added to the phases 1648-1793 on the author's correction; rough box. Podolia and Red Ruthenia boxes (48.2-50.7N, 22.0-29.0E) added to 1648-1699 on the author's correction (Kamianets stayed Polish until 1672). Cell 37 (Dniester, 47.75N 29.6E) added 1569-1648: rough fill of a gap.

Volhynia, Galicia and Red Ruthenia; Ottoman Podillia and the Cossack Hetmanate excluded

polities.name: Habsburg Galicia, Bukovina and Transcarpathia
polities.note: Rough rule of the pile territory.

polities.name: Russian Empire (Ukrainian governorates)
polities.note: Boundaries by date from the treaties (my own knowledge, not re-read on Wikipedia); the footprints are boxes on the grid. Empire from 1721; Left Bank and Kyiv; the Sich lands from 1775; Crimea and the steppe from 1783; Yedisan to the Dniester 1792; Right Bank 1793-95; Budjak and Khotyn 1812.

phases.label: to the Austrian and Romanian borders

polities.name: Kingdom of Hungary (Transcarpathia)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Held Transcarpathia from the 10th-11th century until 1918 (inside Austria-Hungary from 1867); only the Ukrainian part is in the footprint.

maps.t: Category: Maps of the Kingdom of Hungary

polities.name: Principality of Transylvania (Transcarpathia)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Vassal of the Ottomans and later under the Habsburgs; its princes (Rákóczi, Bethlen) held parts of Transcarpathia (Mukachevo).

maps.t: 1570 borders of the Principality of Transylvania.svg
Category: Maps of the history of Transylvania

polities.name: Hungarian Soviet Republic (Transcarpathia)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Hungarian Red Army held part of Transcarpathia for a few weeks in 1919; the Uzhhorod area was the Hungarian side of the front.

maps.t: Category: Maps of the Hungarian Soviet Republic

polities.name: Czechoslovakia (Subcarpathian Rus)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Subcarpathian Rus joined Czechoslovakia in May 1919 (Saint-Germain treaty); autonomous from Oct 1938 (see Carpatho-Ukraine), occupied by Hungary on 15-18 Mar 1939.

maps.t: Category: Maps of the Subcarpathian Rus (1919-1938)

polities.name: Kingdom of Hungary (1939-1944, Transcarpathia)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Hungary annexed Carpatho-Ukraine in March 1939 and held it until Oct 1944.

maps.t: Category: Maps of Hungary during World War II

polities.name: Transcarpathian Ukraine (1944-1946)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Red Army and the People's Council (Nov 1944), manifesto for union with Soviet Ukraine; ceded by Czechoslovakia on 29 Jun 1945, a province of the Ukrainian SSR from Jan 1946.

polities.name: Hutsul Republic
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. January-June 1919, centred on Yasinia and Rakhiv, in the Hutsul Carpathians; Romanian and Czechoslovak troops ended it.

polities.name: Lemko Republics (Komancza and Florynka)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Komancza Republic (Nov 1918-Jan 1919) and Lemko-Rusyn Republic at Florynka (Dec 1918-Mar 1920): in the Lemko region, outside modern Ukraine, so given as points.

polities.name: Rusyn National Councils (1918-1919)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Local councils in Uzhhorod, Prešov, Khust and Lubovnia in 1918-19 that decided whether to join Ukraine, Hungary, Czechoslovakia or Russia; Khust council voted for union with Ukraine on 21 Jan 1919.

maps.t: Category: Maps of the Subcarpathian Rus (1919-1938)

polities.name: Principality of Moldavia (Ukrainian lands)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Held Bukovina and Pokuttia (till 1531), Khotyn and, at times, Budjak; Bukovina passed to Austria in 1775.

maps.t: Historical Atlas of Ukraine, "Ukrainian lands circa 1400" (printed map; page and edition not recorded)
Category: Maps of the Principality of Moldavia

polities.name: Moldavian Democratic Republic
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Bessarabia, 1917-18 (on your December 1917 map as MDR); united with Romania on 9 Apr 1918. Of its territory the grid holds Budjak and the Khotyn area.

polities.name: Kingdom of Romania (Bukovina, Bessarabia)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Bessarabia from Mar-Apr 1918, Bukovina from Nov 1918; Northern Bukovina and Southern Bessarabia went to the USSR in Jun 1940; Romania held them again Jun 1941-1944.

maps.t: Map of the Kingdom of Romania in 1930.gif

polities.name: Transnistria Governorate
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Romanian administration between the Dniester and the Southern Bug (capital Odesa), 1941-44.

polities.name: Odesa Soviet Republic
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Jan-Mar 1918; Odesa area; rough box.

polities.name: Ukrainian People's Republic of Soviets
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Soviet counter-government proclaimed in Kharkiv on 25 Dec 1917; held the Left Bank and Donbas in early 1918.

polities.name: Donetsk-Kryvyi Rih Soviet Republic
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Feb-Mar 1918: Donbas, Kryvyi Rih and Kharkiv governorate parts; rough box.

polities.name: Free Territory (Makhnovshchina)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Anarchist-controlled steppe around Huliaipole. Two tiers, after the Wikipedia map 'Location of the Makhnovshchina': a core (held) around Huliaipole, Berdiansk and the Dnipro bend, and a wider area of influence (claimed, dotted) from Kherson steppe to the Donets and north to Katerynoslav and Izium. The extent changed a lot: widest mid-1919 and autumn 1919, much reduced in 1920-21 (needs a historian).

polities.name: Crimean People's Republic
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Proclaimed by the Kurultai on 26 Dec 1917; ended by the Bolsheviks in Jan 1918 (on your map as the Kurultai).

polities.name: Taurida Soviet Socialist Republic
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Mar-Apr 1918, Crimea.

polities.name: Crimean Regional Government
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Apr 1918-Apr 1919, under German protection, then Allied; Crimea only.

maps.t: Crimea during the Russian Civil War

polities.name: South Russia (Denikin)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Armed Forces of South Russia, 1919; held south and east Ukraine, Kyiv (Aug-Dec 1919), Crimea. Roughly all of the Russian-Empire part of Ukraine at the peak.

maps.t: GC of the Armed Forces of South Russia Map.png

polities.name: Wrangel's Crimea (Russian State)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Apr-Nov 1920: Crimea and northern Tavria.

maps.t: Crimea during the Russian Civil War

polities.name: Second Polish Republic (Galicia and Volhynia)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Galicia from Jul 1919, western Volhynia from 1921 (Treaty of Riga: Zbruch and Sluch); to Sept 1939. Lemko region and Kholm as points.

maps.t: Category: Maps of the Second Polish Republic

polities.name: Autonomous Republic of Crimea
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. 1991-2014 inside independent Ukraine.

polities.name: Crimean ASSR
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Autonomous republic inside the RSFSR, 1921-45 (Tatars deported in May 1944).

polities.name: Crimean Oblast (RSFSR)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. 1945-54 an oblast of the RSFSR; transferred to the Ukrainian SSR on 19 Feb 1954.

polities.name: Unlawfully occupied Crimea
polities.note: Territory of Ukraine unlawfully occupied by Russia since Feb-Mar 2014; the annexation is not recognised under international law. Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia.

maps.t: Category: Maps of the annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation

polities.name: Taurida Governorate
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Crimea and northern Tavria (Melitopol, Berdiansk), from the annexation of the Khanate; Oblast 1783-96, Governorate from 1802.

polities.name: Nogai Hordes (Budjak and Yedisan)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Nomads in the steppe between the Danube and the Bug, vassals of the Crimean Khanate and the Ottomans until the Russian conquest (1789-1812).

polities.name: Principality of Theodoro
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Orthodox principality of south-west Crimea, capital Mangup; as points.

maps.t: Category: Maps of Principality of Theodoro

polities.name: Genoese Gazaria
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Genoese trading colonies on the Crimean and Azov coast (Caffa, Sudak, Cembalo); as points.

polities.name: Black Sea and Kuban Cossack Hosts
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Former Zaporozhian Cossacks resettled on the Kuban (1792-93); Black Sea Host to 1860, then Kuban Host; outside the grid, as points.

maps.t: KOZAKS of the BLACK SEA on the MAP of 1806.JPG

polities.name: Zaporozhian Sich (Zaporozhian Host)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Cossack republic below the Dnipro rapids, to its destruction by Russia in June 1775; the Wild Fields (rough box).

polities.name: Sloboda Ukraine
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Settled from the 1630s-50s; Sloboda Ukraine Governorate 1765-1835 (Kharkiv).

maps.t: Category: Maps of Sloboda Ukraine Governorate

polities.name: New Russia (Novorossiya Governorate)
polities.note: Boundaries by date from the treaties (my own knowledge, not re-read on Wikipedia); the footprints are boxes on the grid. 1764-83 only the military colonies (New Serbia around Kropyvnytskyi, Slavo-Serbia), then the whole southern steppe; the Right Bank (Uman) stayed Polish until 1793.

phases.label: the steppe south of 48.8 N, east of 31 E

polities.name: Little Russia Governorate
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Chernihiv, Poltava and Kyiv left bank after the abolition of the Hetmanate (1764); Little Russia general-governorship 1802-56; rough rule.

polities.name: Muscovy and the Tsardom of Russia (Ukrainian lands)
polities.note: Boundaries by date from the treaties (my own knowledge, not re-read on Wikipedia); the footprints are boxes on the grid. 1503-1618 Chernihiv-Siversk lands (treaty of Moscow; lost to the Commonwealth by Deulino 1618); from the Pereiaslav agreement (1654) the Hetmanate was under the Tsar, and from Andrusovo (1667) the Left Bank and Kyiv (confirmed by the Eternal Peace, 1686) were Russian-held.

aliases: Crown of the Kingdom of Poland
polities.note: Boundaries by date from the treaties (my own knowledge, not re-read on Wikipedia); the footprints are boxes on the grid. Galicia from 1340-87 (Ruthenian Voivodeship 1434); western Podillia from 1430-34 (Podolian Voivodeship).

polities.name: Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria (Austria)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Habsburg crown land of Galicia, 1772-1918 (Lviv); Eastern Galicia in the grid.

polities.name: Duchy of Bukovina (Austria)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Annexed from Moldavia in 1774-75, a crown land from 1849 (Czernowitz).

polities.name: Principality of Halych
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Principality of the Rostyslavychi, after 1141 united under Halych (Yaroslav Osmomysl); rough box.

polities.name: Principality of Volhynia
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Volodymyr-Volynskyi; united with Halych in 1199; rough box.

polities.name: Principality of Kyiv
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Kyiv land after the fragmentation of Rus (from 1132); to 1362 under Lithuania, to 1471 an appanage, then the Kyiv Voivodeship.

polities.name: Principality of Chernihiv
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Chernihiv and Siversk lands; to Lithuania in 1360s-1401; rough box.

polities.name: Principality of Pereiaslav
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Frontier principality on the steppe; destroyed by the Mongols (1239-1302); rough box.

polities.name: District Galicia (General Government)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Nazi civil administration of Eastern Galicia (Lemberg), Aug 1941-Jul 1944, inside the General Government.

maps.t: Category: Maps of Ukraine in World War II

polities.name: Ukrainian State (30 June 1941)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Proclaimed in Lviv by the OUN-B; suppressed by the Germans within weeks.

polities.name: Unlawfully occupied Donetsk and Luhansk (Russian puppet "DNR" and "LNR")
polities.uk: Незаконно окуповані Донеччина і Луганщина («ДНР» і «ЛНР»)
polities.note: Territory of Ukraine unlawfully occupied by Russia: the "DNR" and "LNR" are Russian-controlled puppet entities that no state recognises as lawful, and Russia's declared annexation of 30 Sept 2022 is void under international law. Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. 2014-22 east Donbas, then the occupied south-east.

polities.name: Russian Republic (Provisional Government)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Mar-Nov 1917; the Ukrainian Central Rada was autonomous within it from the Second Universal (Jul 1917) and the Provisional Government ended with the October coup.

polities.name: Wild Fields (Tatar and Nogai steppe)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. The thinly settled steppe south and east of the Lithuanian, Polish and Muscovite frontiers, under the nominal suzerainty of the Crimean Khanate and the Nogais; it is drawn last, so every state that held a cell (the Sich from 1552, Sloboda Ukraine, the Khanate) shows instead.

polities.name: Magyar tribes (Etelköz)
polities.note: Rough rule, not yet checked against Wikipedia: the Hungarian tribal union in the Pontic steppe before it moved into the Carpathian Basin (about 895); the western steppe.

polities.name: Khazar Khaganate (steppe)
polities.note: Rough rule, not yet checked against Wikipedia: the eastern steppe and the Crimean steppe until the campaigns of Sviatoslav (about 965); in Crimea (Kerch) a Khazar remnant until the Byzantine-Rus expedition of 1016.

polities.name: Pecheneg Khanates
polities.note: Rough rule, not yet checked against Wikipedia: the steppe from the Danube to the Don; dominant from about 900 until the Cumans (1055). Defeated by Yaroslav at Kyiv in 1036.

polities.name: Cumans (Polovtsians, Cuman-Kipchak)
polities.note: Rough rule, not yet checked against Wikipedia: the steppe from the Danube to the Don until the Mongol conquest (1237 to 1240).

polities.name: Tmutarakan
polities.note: Rough rule, not yet checked against Wikipedia: a Rus principality on the Taman and Kerch peninsulas (outside the grid), as a point.

polities.name: Byzantine Cherson (Crimea)
polities.note: Rough rule, not yet checked against Wikipedia: the Byzantine theme of Cherson on the south-west coast of Crimea; the end is taken as 1204 (after which it was only nominally Byzantine).

polities.name: Red Ruthenia (Ruthenian and Belz voivodeships)
polities.note: Historical region centred on Galicia (Lviv, Przemysl, Belz, Halych, Sanok, Zhovkva), spanning parts of western Ukraine and south-eastern Poland. Dates are those of the Ruthenian Voivodeship (1434) to the First Partition (1772). Rough box 48.7-50.7 N, 22.0-26.3 E, not yet checked against a map. Its extent varied by period and author; the term usually means the former Principality of Halych and the Ruthenian and Belz voivodeships (Encyclopedia of Ukraine). Because the map colours a cell by the shortest-lived state that holds it, this long-lived region never takes a cell colour; it is used to link records and headings. Sources named by the author, not all read: Ruwiki article "Червонная Русь" (ru.ruwiki.ru, could not be fetched), Encyclopedia of Ukraine, maps by Sanson (1701) and Moll (18th century) on Wikimedia Commons.

polities.name: Crimean Socialist Soviet Republic
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Bolshevik rule in Crimea, April to June 1919.

polities.name: Soviet Crimea (Crimean Revolutionary Committee)
polities.note: Rough rule from general knowledge, not yet checked against Wikipedia. Crimea after Wrangel (November 1920) until the Crimean ASSR was proclaimed in October 1921.
